properties.name: Time of Day String
properties.description:
This variable displays the Time of Day float as a string with hours/minutes formatting. You can also type a new value to set the Time of Day using a correctly formatted string.
(To control Time of Day this way at runtime, call the function "Set Time of Day With String". To get time formatted this way at runtime, you can call "Get Time of Day as String".)

     12 Hour Time formats:
12:34 XM
12:34XM
12:34:56 XM
12:34:56XM
12XM
12 XM
     24 Hour Time formats:
12:34
12:34:56
12

A padding 0 for the hour can be included or left out without issue. AM and PM letters are case insensitive.

properties.name: Project Mode
properties.description: Determines how the system will behave at runtime. Game / Real-time mode allows the system to optimize and spread out some of its runtime calculations, to reduce load on the game thread. Cinematic / Offline mode bypasses these optimizations so that nearly everything on the sky does a complete update every frame at runtime. Cinematic mode also automatically adjusts some quality settings at runtime for maximum quality while rendering. See the Cinematic/Offline Rendering category for settings to adjust the specifics of those quality adjustments.

properties.name: Animate Time of Day
properties.description:
If this is enabled, Time of Day will move forward at runtime, to create a day/night cycle. If the sun's mobility is not movable, this has no effect.

Note, in Unreal Engine having light sources in constant motion can incur extra rendering costs that have nothing to do with UDS specifically, like the cost of cached virtual shadow maps being redrawn when light sources move. Keep this in mind when making performance considerations in a game with a dynamic time of day.

If enabled, all tick logic on UDS and UDW will be staggered to only happen every other frame. How this works depends on if UDS is used alone or alongside UDW:
UDS Alone: Frame A runs first half of UDS tick logic. Frame B runs second half of UDS tick logic.
UDS and UDW: Frame A runs UDW tick logic. Frame B runs UDS tick logic.

Only applied if the framerate is above the threshold set by Half Rate Tick Framerate Threshold.

This does not apply if Project Mode is set to Cinematic / Offline.

properties.name: Sunset/Sunrise Color (Absorption)
properties.description: This is used to set the Absorption variable on the Sky Atmosphere component, which mainly has the effect of tinting the sky color when the sun or moon is low in the sky. Can be used in conjuction with the intensity value below to achieve dramatically colored sunsets. Also note that this color isn't delivered directly to the sky atmosphere, but has its hue inverted first. This is because the actual color for absorption will be the opposite of the one visible, because the absorbed light is what the value represents. So this inverting is done for convenience.

It's mainly intended as a cheaper replacement for volumetric fog effects. With this setting you can decide if you want it enabled only when volumetric fog is off, enabled always, or disabled always.

properties.name: Enable Radial Storm Spawning
properties.description:
Enable to have UDW spawn in Radial Storm actors periodically, which will move across the level, passing over the player's location.
Note, because radial storms occupy a specific location and they will be spawned to intersect the player's location (specifically the Control Point Location, configurable in Basic Controls) this is not a feature which will make much sense in a multiplayer context in a very large open world level where players could be spread very far from one another. properties.display_name: Override Path Tracing Include Indirect Diffuse

properties.name: bMobileHQGaussian
properties.display_name: High Quality Gaussian DoF on Mobile
properties.description: Enable HQ Gaussian on high end mobile platforms. (ES3_1)

properties.name: BloomMethod
properties.description: Preferred bloom algorithm. A different method may be used if the preferred method is not available on the target platform, e.g. due to performance limits.

properties.name: AutoExposureMethod
properties.description: Luminance computation method

properties.name: TemperatureType
properties.description:
Selects the type of temperature calculation.
White Balance uses the Temperature value to control the virtual camera's White Balance. This is the default selection.
Color Temperature uses the Temperature value to adjust the color temperature of the scene, which is the inverse of the White Balance operation.

properties.name: WhiteTemp
properties.description: Controls the color temperature or white balance in degrees Kelvin which the scene considers as white light.

properties.name: WhiteTint
properties.description: Controls the color of the scene along the magenta - green axis (orthogonal to the color temperature).  This feature is equivalent to color tint in digital cameras.

properties.name: ColorSaturation
properties.description: Control the intensity of the color(hue) for the entire image.Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

properties.name: ColorContrast
properties.description: Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

properties.name: ColorGamma
properties.description: Control the luminance curve of the scene. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the entire image.

properties.name: ColorGain
properties.description: This value multiplies the colors of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the entire scene.

properties.name: ColorOffset
properties.description: This value is added to the colors of the scene.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the image being more or less washed-out.

properties.name: ColorSaturationShadows
properties.description: Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the shadow region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

properties.name: ColorContrastShadows
properties.description: Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

properties.name: ColorGammaShadows
properties.description: Control the luminance curve of the shadow region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the shadow region.

properties.name: ColorGainShadows
properties.description: This value multiplies the colors in the shadow region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

properties.name: ColorOffsetShadows
properties.description: This value is added to the colors in the shadow region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the shadows being more or less washed-out.

properties.name: ColorSaturationMidtones
properties.description: Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the mid-tone region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

properties.name: ColorContrastMidtones
properties.description: Control the range of light and dark values in the mid-tone region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

properties.name: ColorGammaMidtones
properties.description: Control the luminance curve of the mid-tone region of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the image.

properties.name: ColorGainMidtones
properties.description: This value multiplies the colors in the mid-tone region of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

properties.name: ColorOffsetMidtones
properties.description: This value is added to the colors in the mid-tone region of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the mid-tones being more or less washed-out.

properties.name: ColorSaturationHighlights
properties.description: Control the intensity of the color (hue) for the highlights region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

properties.name: ColorContrastHighlights
properties.description: Control the range of light and dark values in the highlights region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

properties.name: ColorGammaHighlights
properties.description: Control the luminance curve of the highlight region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the highlight region.

properties.name: ColorGainHighlights
properties.description: This value multiplies the colors in the highlight region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

properties.name: ColorOffsetHighlights
properties.description: This value is added to the colors in the highlight region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the highlights being more or less washed-out.

properties.name: ColorCorrectionHighlightsMin
properties.description: This value sets the lower threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.

properties.name: ColorCorrectionHighlightsMax
properties.description: This value sets the upper threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.  This value should be larger than HighlightsMin. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

properties.name: ColorCorrectionShadowsMax
properties.description: This value sets the threshold for what is considered to be the shadow region of the image.

properties.name: BlueCorrection
properties.description: Correct for artifacts with "electric" blues due to the ACEScg color space. Bright blue desaturates instead of going to violet.

properties.name: ExpandGamut
properties.description: Expand bright saturated colors outside the sRGB gamut to fake wide gamut rendering.

properties.name: ToneCurveAmount
properties.description: Allow effect of Tone Curve to be reduced (Set ToneCurveAmount and ExpandGamut to 0.0 to fully disable tone curve)

properties.name: TonemappingMethod
properties.description: Controls the method of tonemapping.

properties.name: FilmSlope
properties.description: Controls the overall steepness of the tonemapper curve.  Larger values increase scene contrast and smaller values reduce contrast.

properties.name: FilmToe
properties.description: Controls the contrast of the dark end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

properties.name: FilmShoulder
properties.description: Sometimes referred to as highlight rolloff.  Controls the contrast of the bright end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

properties.name: FilmBlackClip
properties.description: Lowers the toe of the tonemapper curve by this amount. Increasing this value causes more of the scene to clip to black.  For most purposes, this property should remain 0

properties.name: FilmWhiteClip
properties.description: Controls the height of the tonemapper curve.  Raising this value can cause bright values to more quickly approach fully-saturated white.

properties.name: SceneColorTint
properties.description: Scene tint color

properties.name: SceneFringeIntensity
properties.description: in percent, Scene chromatic aberration / color fringe (camera imperfection) to simulate an artifact that happens in real-world lens, mostly visible in the image corners.

properties.name: ChromaticAberrationStartOffset
properties.description: A normalized distance to the center of the framebuffer where the effect takes place.

properties.name: BloomIntensity
properties.description: Multiplier for all bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

properties.name: BloomGaussianIntensity
properties.description: Multiplier for Gaussian bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

properties.name: BloomThreshold
properties.description:
minimum brightness the bloom starts having effect
-1:all pixels affect bloom equally (physically correct, faster as a threshold pass is omitted), 0:all pixels affect bloom brights more, 1(default), >1 brighter

properties.name: BloomSizeScale
properties.description: Scale for all bloom sizes

properties.name: Bloom1Size
properties.description:
Diameter size for the Bloom1 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/2 resolution, larger values cost more performance, good for high frequency details)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

properties.name: Bloom2Size
properties.description:
Diameter size for Bloom2 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/4 resolution, larger values cost more performance)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

properties.name: Bloom3Size
properties.description:
Diameter size for Bloom3 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/8 resolution, larger values cost more performance)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

properties.name: Bloom4Size
properties.description:
Diameter size for Bloom4 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/16 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

properties.name: Bloom5Size
properties.description:
Diameter size for Bloom5 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/32 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

properties.name: Bloom6Size
properties.description:
Diameter size for Bloom6 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/64 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

properties.name: Bloom1Tint
properties.description: Bloom1 tint color

properties.name: Bloom2Tint
properties.description: Bloom2 tint color

properties.name: Bloom3Tint
properties.description: Bloom3 tint color

properties.name: Bloom4Tint
properties.description: Bloom4 tint color

properties.name: Bloom5Tint
properties.description: Bloom5 tint color

properties.name: Bloom6Tint
properties.description: Bloom6 tint color

properties.name: BloomConvolutionIntensity
properties.description: Multiplier for Convolution bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

properties.name: BloomConvolutionScatterDispersion
properties.description: Intensity multiplier on the scatter dispersion energy of the kernel. 1.0 means exactly use the same energy as the kernel scatter dispersion.

properties.name: BloomConvolutionSize
properties.description: Relative size of the convolution kernel image compared to the minor axis of the viewport

properties.name: BloomConvolutionTexture
properties.description: Texture to replace default convolution bloom kernel

properties.name: BloomConvolutionCenterUV
properties.description: The UV location of the center of the kernel.  Should be very close to (.5,.5)

properties.name: BloomConvolutionPreFilterMin
properties.description: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

properties.name: BloomConvolutionPreFilterMax
properties.description: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

properties.name: BloomConvolutionPreFilterMult
properties.description: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

properties.name: BloomConvolutionBufferScale
properties.description: Implicit buffer region as a fraction of the screen size to insure the bloom does not wrap across the screen.  Larger sizes have perf impact.

properties.name: BloomDirtMask
properties.description: Texture that defines the dirt on the camera lens where the light of very bright objects is scattered.

properties.name: BloomDirtMaskIntensity
properties.description: BloomDirtMask intensity

properties.name: BloomDirtMaskTint
properties.description: BloomDirtMask tint color

properties.name: DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod
properties.description: Chooses the Dynamic Global Illumination method.  Not compatible with Forward Shading.

properties.name: IndirectLightingColor
properties.description: Adjusts indirect lighting color. (1,1,1) is default. (0,0,0) to disable GI. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

properties.name: IndirectLightingIntensity
properties.description: Scales the indirect lighting contribution. A value of 0 disables GI. Default is 1. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

properties.name: LumenRayLightingMode
properties.description: Controls how Lumen rays are lit when Lumen is using Hardware Ray Tracing.  By default, Lumen uses the Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to 'Hit Lighting' for higher quality.

properties.name: LumenSceneLightingQuality
properties.description: Scales Lumen Scene's quality.  Larger scales cause Lumen Scene to be calculated with a higher fidelity, which can be visible in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenSceneDetail
properties.description: Controls the size of instances that can be represented in Lumen Scene.  Larger values will ensure small objects are represented, but increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenSceneViewDistance
properties.description: Sets the maximum view distance of the scene that Lumen maintains for ray tracing against.  Larger values will increase the effective range of sky shadowing and Global Illumination, but increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeed
properties.description: Controls how much Lumen Scene is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance.  Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenFinalGatherQuality
properties.description: Scales Lumen's Final Gather quality.  Larger scales reduce noise, but greatly increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenFinalGatherLightingUpdateSpeed
properties.description: Controls how much Lumen Final Gather is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance.  Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost and noise.

properties.name: LumenFinalGatherScreenTraces
properties.description: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Global Illumination. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

properties.name: LumenMaxTraceDistance
properties.description: Controls the maximum distance that Lumen should trace while solving lighting.  Values that are too small will cause lighting to leak into large caves, while values that are large will increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenDiffuseColorBoost
properties.description: Allows brightening indirect lighting by calculating material diffuse color for indirect lighting. Values above 1 (original diffuse color) aren't physically correct, but they can be useful as an art direction knob to increase the amount of bounced light in the scene. Best to keep below 2 as it also causes reflections to be brighter than the scene.

properties.name: LumenAmbientOcclusionIntensity
properties.description: Allows control over the strength of Lumen's Short Range Ambient Occlusion.

properties.name: LumenSkylightLeaking
properties.description: Controls what fraction of the skylight intensity should be allowed to leak.  This can be useful as an art direction knob (non-physically based) to keep indoor areas from going fully black.

properties.name: LumenSkylightLeakingTint
properties.description: Color tint for Lumen Skylight Leaking.

properties.name: LumenFullSkylightLeakingDistance
properties.description: Controls the distance from a receiving surface where skylight leaking reaches its full intensity.  Smaller values make the skylight leaking flatter, while larger values create an Ambient Occlusion effect.

properties.name: LumenSurfaceCacheResolution
properties.description: Scale factor for Lumen Surface Cache resolution.  Smaller values save GPU memory, at a cost in quality.  Defaults to 0.5 for Scene Captures if not overridden.

properties.name: ReflectionMethod
properties.description: Chooses the Reflection method. Not compatible with Forward Shading.

properties.name: LumenReflectionQuality
properties.description: Scales the Reflection quality.  Larger scales reduce noise in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenReflectionsScreenTraces
properties.description: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Reflections. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

properties.name: LumenFrontLayerTranslucencyReflections
properties.description: Whether to use high quality mirror reflections on the front layer of translucent surfaces.  Other layers will use the lower quality Radiance Cache method that can only produce glossy reflections.  Increases GPU cost when enabled.

properties.name: LumenMaxRoughnessToTraceReflections
properties.description: Sets the maximum roughness value for which Lumen still traces dedicated reflection rays. Higher values improve reflection quality, but greatly increase GPU cost.

properties.name: LumenMaxReflectionBounces
properties.description: Sets the maximum number of recursive reflection bounces. 1 means a single reflection ray (no secondary reflections in mirrors). Currently only supported by Hardware Ray Tracing with Hit Lighting.

properties.name: LumenMaxRefractionBounces
properties.description: The maximum count of refraction event to trace. When hit lighting is used, Translucent meshes will be traced when LumenMaxRefractionBounces > 0, making the reflection tracing more expenssive.

properties.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionIntensity
properties.description: Enable/Fade/disable the Screen Space Reflection feature, in percent, avoid numbers between 0 and 1 fo consistency

properties.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionQuality
properties.description: 0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition, 50 is the default for better performance.

properties.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness
properties.description: Until what roughness we fade the screen space reflections, 0.8 works well, smaller can run faster

properties.name: bMegaLights
properties.description:
Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights.
MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost.
When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used.
MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

properties.name: MegaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency
properties.description: Whether to use high quality direct lighting on the front layer of translucent surfaces.  Other layers will use the lower quality Translucency Lighting Volume.  Increases GPU cost when enabled.

properties.name: AmbientCubemapTint
properties.description: AmbientCubemap tint color

properties.name: AmbientCubemapIntensity
properties.description:
To scale the Ambient cubemap brightness
>=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

properties.name: AmbientCubemap
properties.description: The Ambient cubemap (Affects diffuse and specular shading), blends additively which if different from all other settings here

properties.name: CameraShutterSpeed
properties.description: The camera shutter in 1/seconds.

properties.name: CameraISO
properties.description: The camera sensor sensitivity

properties.name: DepthOfFieldFstop
properties.description: Defines the opening of the camera lens, Aperture is 1/fstop, typical lens go down to f/1.2 (large opening), larger numbers reduce the DOF effect

properties.name: DepthOfFieldMinFstop
properties.description: Defines the maximum opening of the camera lens to control the curvature of blades of the diaphragm. Set it to 0 to get straight blades.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldBladeCount
properties.description: Defines the number of blades of the diaphragm within the lens (between 4 and 16).

properties.name: AutoExposureBias
properties.description:
Logarithmic adjustment for the exposure. Only used if a tonemapper is specified.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

properties.name: AutoExposureBiasBackup
properties.description:
With the auto exposure changes, we are changing the AutoExposureBias inside the serialization code. We are
storing that value before conversion here as a backup. Hopefully it will not be needed, and removed in the next engine revision.

properties.name: bOverride_AutoExposureBiasBackup
properties.description:
With the auto exposure changes, we are also changing the auto exposure override value, so we are storing
that backup as well.

properties.name: AutoExposureApplyPhysicalCameraExposure
properties.description: Only affects Manual exposure mode.

properties.name: AutoExposureBiasCurve
properties.description:
Exposure compensation based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate the final exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

properties.name: AutoExposureMeterMask
properties.description:
Exposure metering mask. Bright spots on the mask will have high influence on auto-exposure metering
and dark spots will have low influence.

properties.name: AutoExposureLowPercent
properties.description:
The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color.
The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority
but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of
bright spots.
>0, <100, good values are in the range 70 .. 80

properties.name: AutoExposureHighPercent
properties.description:
The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color.
The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority
but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of
bright spots.
>0, <100, good values are in the range 80 .. 95

properties.name: AutoExposureMinBrightness
properties.description:
Auto-Exposure minimum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max.
Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value.
The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

properties.name: AutoExposureMaxBrightness
properties.description:
Auto-Exposure maximum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max.
Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value.
The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

properties.name: AutoExposureSpeedUp
properties.description: In F-stops per second, should be >0

properties.name: AutoExposureSpeedDown
properties.description: In F-stops per second, should be >0

properties.name: HistogramLogMin
properties.description: Histogram Min value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

properties.name: HistogramLogMax
properties.description: Histogram Max value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

properties.name: AutoExposureCalibrationConstant
properties.description: Calibration constant for 18% albedo, deprecating this value.

properties.name: LocalExposureMethod
properties.description: Local Exposure algorithm

properties.name: LocalExposureHighlightContrastScale
properties.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value.
Value less than 1 will enable local exposure.
Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

properties.name: LocalExposureShadowContrastScale
properties.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value.
Value less than 1 will enable local exposure.
Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

properties.name: LocalExposureHighlightContrastCurve
properties.description:
Local Exposure Highlight Contrast based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

properties.name: LocalExposureShadowContrastCurve
properties.description:
Local Exposure Shadow Contrast based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

properties.name: LocalExposureHighlightThreshold
properties.description: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered highlights.

properties.name: LocalExposureShadowThreshold
properties.description: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered shadows.

properties.name: LocalExposureDetailStrength
properties.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Value different than 1 will enable local exposure.
This value should be set to 1 in most cases.

properties.name: LocalExposureBlurredLuminanceBlend
properties.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Blend between bilateral filtered and blurred luminance as the base layer.
Blurred luminance helps preserve image appearance and specular highlights, and reduce ringing.
Good values are usually in the range 0.4 .. 0.6

properties.name: LocalExposureBlurredLuminanceKernelSizePercent
properties.description: Kernel size (percentage of screen) used to blur frame luminance.

properties.name: LocalExposureHighlightThresholdStrength
properties.description: Strength of the highlight threshold.

properties.name: LocalExposureShadowThresholdStrength
properties.description: Strength of the shadow threshold.

properties.name: LocalExposureMiddleGreyBias
properties.description:
Logarithmic adjustment for the local exposure middle grey.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

properties.name: LensFlareIntensity
properties.description: Brightness scale of the image cased lens flares (linear)

properties.name: LensFlareTint
properties.description: Tint color for the image based lens flares.

properties.name: LensFlareBokehSize
properties.description: Size of the Lens Blur (in percent of the view width) that is done with the Bokeh texture (note: performance cost is radius*radius)

properties.name: LensFlareThreshold
properties.description: Minimum brightness the lens flare starts having effect (this should be as high as possible to avoid the performance cost of blurring content that is too dark too see)

properties.name: LensFlareBokehShape
properties.description: Defines the shape of the Bokeh when the image base lens flares are blurred, cannot be blended

properties.name: LensFlareTints
properties.description: RGB defines the lens flare color, A it's position. This is a temporary solution.

properties.name: VignetteIntensity
properties.description: 0..1 0=off/no vignette .. 1=strong vignette

properties.name: VignetteType
properties.description: The shape type of the vignette

properties.name: VignetteCenter
properties.description: Position of the vignette center in UV space.

properties.name: VignetteColor
properties.description: Color multiplied with areas that are masked by the vignette. Default is black.

properties.name: VignetteSize
properties.description: Scale of the vignette shape in screenspace. Can be used to scale vignette anamorphically. Default is 1.

properties.name: VignetteSoftness
properties.description: The softness of the transition from opaque to transparant on the edge of the vignette shape.

properties.name: VignetteTexture
properties.description: Defines the shape of the vignette when VignetteType is set to Texture

properties.name: Sharpen
properties.description: Controls the strength of image sharpening applied during tonemapping.

properties.name: FilmGrainIntensity
properties.description: 0..1 Film grain intensity to apply. LinearSceneColor *= lerp(1.0, DecodedFilmGrainTexture, FilmGrainIntensity)

properties.name: FilmGrainIntensityShadows
properties.description: Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered shadow areas.

properties.name: FilmGrainIntensityMidtones
properties.description: Control over the grain intensity in the mid-tone region of the image.

properties.name: FilmGrainIntensityHighlights
properties.description: Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered highlight areas.

properties.name: FilmGrainShadowsMax
properties.description: Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Shadow Intensity.

properties.name: FilmGrainHighlightsMin
properties.description: Sets the lower bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity.

properties.name: FilmGrainHighlightsMax
properties.description: Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity. This value should be larger than HighlightsMin.. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

properties.name: FilmGrainScale
properties.description: Controls the size of the film grain. Size of texel of FilmGrainTexture on screen.

properties.name: FilmGrainTexture
properties.description: Defines film grain texture to use.

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionIntensity
properties.description: 0..1 0=off/no ambient occlusion .. 1=strong ambient occlusion, defines how much it affects the non direct lighting after base pass

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionStaticFraction
properties.description: 0..1 0=no effect on static lighting .. 1=AO affects the stat lighting, 0 is free meaning no extra rendering pass

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionRadius
properties.description: >0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionRadiusInWS
properties.description: true: AO radius is in world space units, false: AO radius is locked the view space in 400 units

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionFadeDistance
properties.description: >0, in unreal units, at what distance the AO effect disppears in the distance (avoding artifacts and AO effects on huge object)

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionFadeRadius
properties.description: >0, in unreal units, how many units before AmbientOcclusionFadeOutDistance it starts fading out

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionDistance
properties.description: >0, in unreal units, how wide the ambient occlusion effect should affect the geometry (in depth), will be removed - only used for non normal method which is not exposed

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionPower
properties.description: >0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionBias
properties.description: >0, in unreal units, default (3.0) works well for flat surfaces but can reduce details

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionQuality
properties.description: 0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionMipBlend
properties.description: Affects the blend over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions) , 0:fully use full resolution, 1::fully use low resolution, around 0.6 seems to be a good value

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionMipScale
properties.description: Affects the radius AO radius scale over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionMipThreshold
properties.description: to tweak the bilateral upsampling when using multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

properties.name: AmbientOcclusionTemporalBlendWeight
properties.description: How much to blend the current frame with previous frames when using GTAO with temporal accumulation

properties.name: RayTracingAO
properties.description: Enables ray tracing ambient occlusion.

properties.name: RayTracingAOSamplesPerPixel
properties.description: Sets the samples per pixel for ray tracing ambient occlusion.

properties.name: RayTracingAOIntensity
properties.description: Scalar factor on the ray-tracing ambient occlusion score.

properties.name: RayTracingAORadius
properties.description: Defines the world-space search radius for occlusion rays.

properties.name: ColorGradingIntensity
properties.description: Color grading lookup table intensity. 0 = no intensity, 1=full intensity

properties.name: ColorGradingLUT
properties.description: Look up table texture to use or none of not used

properties.name: DepthOfFieldEnabled
properties.description: When false, post-process depth of field will not be used. When true, DoF may be used depending on lens and scalability settings.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldSensorWidth
properties.description: Width of the camera sensor to assume, in mm.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldSqueezeFactor
properties.description: This is the squeeze factor for the DOF, which emulates the properties of anamorphic lenses.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldFocalDistance
properties.description: Distance in which the Depth of Field effect should be sharp, in unreal units (cm)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldDepthBlurAmount
properties.description: CircleDOF only: Depth blur km for 50%

properties.name: DepthOfFieldDepthBlurRadius
properties.description: CircleDOF only: Depth blur radius in pixels at 1920x

properties.name: DepthOfFieldUseHairDepth
properties.description: For depth of field to use the hair depth for computing circle of confusion size. Otherwise use an interpolated distance between the hair depth and the scene depth based on the hair coverage (default).

properties.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalBokeh
properties.description: Simulate stretching in blur and bokeh. Positive values for sagittal (swirly bokeh), negative values for tangential.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalBokehFalloff
properties.description: How quickly does the Petzval bokeh effect increase towards the edge of the image

properties.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxExtents
properties.description: Box, centered on screen, around which the Petzval effect is applied.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxRadius
properties.description: Corner radius

properties.name: DepthOfFieldAspectRatioScalar
properties.description: Amount to scale the output viewport's aspect ratio by when computing depth of field properties.

properties.name: DepthOfFieldBarrelRadius
properties.description: The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

properties.name: DepthOfFieldBarrelLength
properties.description: The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

properties.name: DepthOfFieldMatteBoxFlags
properties.description: Panels around the front of the lens barrel that occlude bokeh

properties.name: DepthOfFieldFocalRegion
properties.description: Artificial region where all content is in focus, starting after DepthOfFieldFocalDistance, in unreal units  (cm)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldNearTransitionRegion
properties.description: To define the width of the transition region next to the focal region on the near side (cm)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldFarTransitionRegion
properties.description: To define the width of the transition region next to the focal region on the near side (cm)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldScale
properties.description:
SM5: BokehDOF only: To amplify the depth of field effect (like aperture)  0=off
          ES3_1: Used to blend DoF. 0=off

properties.name: DepthOfFieldNearBlurSize
properties.description: Gaussian only: Maximum size of the Depth of Field blur (in percent of the view width) (note: performance cost scales with size)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldFarBlurSize
properties.description: Gaussian only: Maximum size of the Depth of Field blur (in percent of the view width) (note: performance cost scales with size)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldOcclusion
properties.description: Occlusion tweak factor 1 (0.18 to get natural occlusion, 0.4 to solve layer color leaking issues)

properties.name: DepthOfFieldSkyFocusDistance
properties.description: Artificial distance to allow the skybox to be in focus (e.g. 200000), <=0 to switch the feature off, only for GaussianDOF, can cost performance

properties.name: DepthOfFieldVignetteSize
properties.description: Artificial circular mask to (near) blur content outside the radius, only for GaussianDOF, diameter in percent of screen width, costs performance if the mask is used, keep Feather can Radius on default to keep it off

properties.name: MotionBlurAmount
properties.description: Strength of motion blur, 0:off

properties.name: MotionBlurMax
properties.description: max distortion caused by motion blur, in percent of the screen width, 0:off

properties.name: MotionBlurTargetFPS
properties.description:
Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative
to the specified target FPS instead. Higher target FPS results in shorter frames, which means shorter
shutter times and less motion blur. Lower FPS means more motion blur. A value of zero makes the motion
blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

properties.name: MotionBlurPerObjectSize
properties.description: The minimum projected screen radius for a primitive to be drawn in the velocity pass, percentage of screen width. smaller numbers cause more draw calls, default: 4%

properties.name: TranslucencyType
properties.description: Sets the translucency type

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyMaxRoughness
properties.description: Sets the maximum roughness until which ray tracing translucency will be visible (lower value is faster). Translucency contribution is smoothly faded when close to roughness threshold. This parameter behaves similarly to ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness.

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyRefractionRays
properties.description: Sets the maximum number of ray tracing refraction rays.

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencySamplesPerPixel
properties.description: Sets the samples per pixel for ray traced translucency.

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyMaxPrimaryHitEvents
properties.description: Maximum number of hit events allowed on primary ray paths

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyMaxSecondaryHitEvents
properties.description: Maximum number of hit events allowed on secondary ray paths

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyShadows
properties.description: Sets the translucency shadows type.

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyRefraction
properties.description: Sets whether refraction should be enabled or not (if not rays will not scatter and only travel in the same direction as before the intersection event).

properties.name: RayTracingTranslucencyUseRayTracedRefraction
properties.description: Whether to use ray traced refraction which currently doesn't work well with rough refraction or simulate it using a screen space effect

properties.name: PathTracingMaxBounces
properties.description: Sets the path tracing maximum bounces

properties.name: PathTracingSamplesPerPixel
properties.description: Sets the samples per pixel for the path tracer.

properties.name: PathTracingMaxPathIntensity
properties.description: Sets the maximum intensity of indirect samples to reduce fireflies. Lowering this value reduces noise at the expense of accuracy. Increasing it is more accurate but may lead to more noise.

properties.name: PathTracingEnableEmissiveMaterials
properties.description: Should emissive materials contribute to scene lighting?

properties.name: PathTracingEnableReferenceDOF
properties.description: Enables a reference quality depth-of-field which replaces the post-process effect.

properties.name: PathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere
properties.description: Enables path tracing in the atmosphere instead of baking the sky atmosphere contribution into a skylight. Any skylight present in the scene will be automatically ignored when this is enabled.

properties.name: PathTracingEnableDenoiser
properties.description: Run the currently loaded denoiser plugin on the last sample to remove noise from the output. Has no effect if a plug-in is not loaded.

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeEmissive
properties.description: Should the render include directly visible emissive elements?

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeDiffuse
properties.description: Should the render include diffuse lighting contributions?

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeIndirectDiffuse
properties.description: Should the render include indirect diffuse lighting contributions?

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeSpecular
properties.description: Should the render include specular lighting contributions?

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeIndirectSpecular
properties.description: Should the render include indirect specular lighting contributions?

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeVolume
properties.description: Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

properties.name: PathTracingIncludeIndirectVolume
properties.description: Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

properties.name: UserFlags
properties.description: Per-view user flags accessible in materials via TestPostVolumeUserFlag node, allowing per-view overrides of material behavior.

properties.name: WeightedBlendables
properties.description:
Allows custom post process materials to be defined, using a MaterialInstance with the same Material as its parent to allow blending.
For materials this needs to be the "PostProcess" domain type. This can be used for any UObject object implementing the IBlendableInterface (e.g. could be used to fade weather settings).

properties.name: PreviewBlendable
properties.description:
For editor material preview windows, we need to support visualizing the output of a blendable that writes to a UserSceneTexture.  Stores
a pointer to a blendable that's being previewed, forcing its output to write to SceneColor instead of the UserSceneTexture, making it visible.

properties.name: Blendables
properties.description: for backwards compatibility

properties.name: Type
properties.description: Holds the type of the bound.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Holds the bound's value.

/Script/Engine.EComponentMobility.name: Static

Static objects cannot be moved or changed in game.
- Allows baked lighting
- Fastest rendering

/Script/Engine.EComponentMobility.name: Stationary
/Script/Engine.EComponentMobility.description:
A stationary light will only have its shadowing and bounced lighting from static geometry baked by Lightmass, all other lighting will be dynamic.

- Can't move

- Dynamic shadows

/Script/Engine.EComponentMobility.name: Movable

Movable objects can be moved and changed in game.
- Totally dynamic
- Can cast dynamic shadows
- Slowest rendering

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator0
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description:
Fidelity + Performance:
This mode prioritizes the resolution of the cloud rendering for good fidelity of cloud details, while keeping the performance cost minimal. Its weaknesses are heavy ghosting in fast movement and low quality sharp intersections with meshes. This mode is ideal for typical scenes where the clouds are a slow moving background element only.

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator1
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description:
Mesh Intersections + Fast Movement + Performance:
This mode prioritizes high quality intersections with meshes and temporal stability in fast movement. It does this with a similar performance cost to "Fidelity + Performance" by sacrificing resolution of the clouds. For this reason the main weakness of this mode is blurry/low detail cloud rendering. This mode is ideal for scenes where the camera needs to go into/above clouds or cloud movement is very fast, and high performance is still a priority.

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator2
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description:
Mesh Intersections + Fast Movement + Fidelity:
This mode has high quality mesh intersections, temporal stability in fast movement, and high resolution cloud rendering for detailed clouds. It is significantly more expensive on the GPU than the first two modes, but could still feasibly be budgeted for in a realtime application targeting higher end hardware.

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator3
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description:
Full Cinematic Quality:
This mode disables the engine's optimizations for volumetric cloud rendering entirely. It will render at full resolution, with no temporal artifacts and perfect mesh intersections. Understand, this mode is NOT for realtime applications. Its extreme cost makes it only reasonable for offline rendering.
Also note, you don't need to select this for best render results if Project Mode is set to Cinematic/Offline. In that mode, Full Cinematic Quality is automatically applied at runtime.

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator2
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description: Determines source of fog colors automatically based on the color mode and the project setting Support Sky Atmosphere Affecting Height Fog. It's recommended to keep this setting. The ideal way to change the source of colors is to change the project setting, not this mode.

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator0
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description: Force the system to use UDS fog color logic, with all the settings below.

/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.name: NewEnumerator1
/Game/UltraDynamicSky/Blueprints/Enum/UD.description: Force the system to try to use sky atmosphere contribution for the fog color.

/Script/Engine.EDynamicGlobalIlluminatio.description: Use Lumen Global Illumination for all lights, emissive materials casting light and SkyLight Occlusion.  Requires 'Generate Mesh Distance Fields' enabled for Software Ray Tracing and 'Support Hardware Ray Tracing' enabled for Hardware Ray Tracing.

/Script/Engine.EDynamicGlobalIlluminatio.name: ScreenSpace
/Script/Engine.EDynamicGlobalIlluminatio.description: Standalone Screen Space Global Illumination.  Low cost, but limited by screen space information.

/Script/Engine.EDynamicGlobalIlluminatio.name: Plugin
/Script/Engine.EDynamicGlobalIlluminatio.description: Use a plugin for Global Illumination

/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.name: SurfaceCache
/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.description: Use Lumen Surface Cache for ray hit lighting. This method gives the best GI and reflection performance, but quality will be limited by how well surface cache represents given scene.

/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.name: HitLightingForReflections
/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.description: Calculate lighting at a hit point for reflections. This will improve reflection quality, but increases GPU cost, as full material needs to be evaluated and shadow rays traced. Lumen Surface Cache will still be used for GI and secondary bounces, including GI seen in reflections.

/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.name: HitLighting
/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.description: Calculate lighting at a hit point for GI and reflections. This will improve both GI and reflection quality, but greatly increases GPU cost, as full material and lighting will be evaluated at every hit point. Lumen Surface Cache will still be used for secondary bounces.

/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.name: ELumenRayLightingModeOverride_MAX
/Script/Engine.ELumenRayLightingModeOver.display_name: ELumen Ray Lighting Mode Override MAX

/Script/Engine.EReflectionMethod.name: None
/Script/Engine.EReflectionMethod.description: No global reflection method will be used. Reflections can still come from Reflection Captures, Planar Reflections or a Skylight placed in the level.

/Script/Engine.EReflectionMethod.name: Lumen
/Script/Engine.EReflectionMethod.description: Use Lumen Reflections, which supports Screen / Software / Hardware Ray Tracing together and integrates with Lumen Global Illumination for rough reflections and Global Illumination seen in reflections.

/Script/Engine.EReflectionMethod.name: ScreenSpace
/Script/Engine.EReflectionMethod.description: Standalone Screen Space Reflections.  Low cost, but limited by screen space information.

/Script/Engine.ELocalExposureMethod.name: Bilateral
/Script/Engine.ELocalExposureMethod.description: Decompose image into base and detail layers using a bilateral blur. Only the base layer contrast is reduced in order to preserve details.

/Script/Engine.ELocalExposureMethod.name: Fusion
/Script/Engine.ELocalExposureMethod.description: Fuse multiple exposures according to quality measures. Local Exposure is calculated using the fused exposures.

/Script/Engine.ETranslucencyType.name: RayTraced_Deprecated
/Script/Engine.ETranslucencyType.description: The legacy Ray Tracing Translucency Method is deprecated, use Ray Traced instead

/Script/Engine.EReflectedAndRefractedRay.name: EReflectedAndRefractedRayTracedShadows_MAX
/Script/Engine.EReflectedAndRefractedRay.display_name: EReflected and Refracted Ray Traced Shadows MAX
